title: Moving DOM Nodes Without Losing State
summary: See how Element.moveBefore() preserves iframe, focus, animation and dialog state when moving DOM nodes, with syntax, constraints, custom element hooks and fallbacks.
body_markdown:
` Element.moveBefore()` moves a node that is already in the document without the remove-then-insert step that` appendChild()` and` insertBefore()` perform, so an` <iframe>` keeps its loaded page, a focused input keeps focus, and a running CSS animation keeps running.


Most developers who reparent live elements have hit this: you drag a card to a new column and the embedded player inside it goes blank and reloads, or the field you were typing in loses focus partway through a word.


[Chrome shipped moveBefore() in Chrome 133](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/movebefore-api) , and the feature appears in the[Chrome 133 release notes](https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/133) as “DOM state-preserving move”. This article covers the syntax, a demo, the exact list of preserved state, the error cases, custom element hooks and a safe fallback. If you need a refresher on the basics first, see[working with the DOM in JavaScript](https://blog.openreplay.com/working-with-the-dom-in-javascript/) and[the life cycle of DOM elements](https://blog.openreplay.com/the-life-cycle-of-dom-elements/) .


## Key Takeaways


- ` parent.moveBefore(node, ref)` takes the same arguments as` insertBefore()` but moves the node without removing and re-inserting it, so iframes, focus, animations, popovers and modal dialogs keep their state.
- The moved node must be an Element or CharacterData node. Moves between documents, between connected and disconnected trees, or into the node’s own descendant throw` HierarchyRequestError` .
- A` MutationObserver` still sees a` moveBefore()` move as one removal and one addition.
- Custom elements that define` connectedMoveCallback()` get that callback instead of` disconnectedCallback()` and` connectedCallback()` .
- Safari does not support` moveBefore()` , so check` 'moveBefore' in Element.prototype` and fall back to` insertBefore()` .


## Why Do appendChild and insertBefore Reset State?


Every move made with` appendChild()` or` insertBefore()` is really two operations: the browser removes the node from the document and then inserts it again. The Chrome team’s launch post points out that the DOM has had no other way to move a node since its early standards. Removing a node tears down state that only exists while the node is connected. An iframe unloads and reloads its document, a focused element loses focus, CSS animations start over, and open popovers and modal dialogs close.


In session replays of reorderable dashboards, the bug usually looks like this: a user drags a card, carries on typing, and the keystrokes don’t land because the field lost focus. Embedded iframes visibly reload in the middle of the session.


## moveBefore() Syntax


` moveBefore()` takes the same two arguments as` insertBefore()` : the node to move and a reference node. Passing` null` as the reference moves the node to the end of the parent’s children.


```text
parent  .  moveBefore  (  movedNode  ,   referenceNode  );
parent  .  moveBefore  (  movedNode  ,   null  );   // append
```


According to[MDN’s moveBefore() reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/moveBefore) , the moved node must be an Element or a CharacterData node. Text nodes are allowed, but document types, for example, are not. The method also exists on[Document](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/moveBefore) and[DocumentFragment](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/DocumentFragment/moveBefore) , so you can move nodes inside a fragment even though a fragment is never connected to the document. The method is defined in the[DOM Living Standard](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-parentnode-movebefore) .


## Demo: Moving an iframe With and Without moveBefore


The quickest way to see the difference is an iframe with its own internal state. This demo uses` srcdoc` , so it makes no network request.


```text
<  div   id  =  "  left  "   class  =  "  box  "  >
<  iframe   id  =  "  frame  "   srcdoc  =  "  <  button onclick='this.textContent=++n'>0  <  /button>  <  script>let n=0  <  /script>  "  ></  iframe  >
</  div  >
<  div   id  =  "  right  "   class  =  "  box  "  ></  div  >
<  button   id  =  "  viaInsert  "  >  Move with insertBefore()  </  button  >
<  button   id  =  "  viaMove  "  >  Move with moveBefore()  </  button  >
<  script  >
const   frame   =   document  .  getElementById  (  '  frame  '  );
const   left   =   document  .  getElementById  (  '  left  '  );
const   right   =   document  .  getElementById  (  '  right  '  );
const   target   =   ()   =>   (  frame  .  parentElement   ===   left   ?   right   :   left  );


document  .  getElementById  (  '  viaInsert  '  ).  onclick   =   ()   =>
target  ().  insertBefore  (  frame  ,   null  );   // iframe reloads, counter back to 0


document  .  getElementById  (  '  viaMove  '  ).  onclick   =   ()   =>
target  ().  moveBefore  (  frame  ,   null  );     // counter value survives
</  script  >
```


Click the counter inside the frame a few times, then try each button.` insertBefore()` reloads the frame and the counter goes back to zero.` moveBefore()` keeps the count. The second button only works in a browser that supports the method (see the feature detection section below).


Focus behaves the same way:


```text
const   input   =   document  .  querySelector  (  '  #note  '  );
input  .  focus  ();
sidebar  .  moveBefore  (  input  ,   null  );
console  .  log  (  document  .  activeElement   ===   input  );   // true
// With sidebar.insertBefore(input, null), focus is lost
```


## What State Does moveBefore() Preserve?


` moveBefore()` keeps a specific set of states, listed on MDN. It does not keep every possible state:


- Animation and transition state
- ` <iframe>` loading state
- ` :focus` and` :active`
- Fullscreen element state
- Popover open state
- Modal` <dialog>` state


Native` <video>` and` <audio>` elements keep their play state even when moved with` appendChild()` or` insertBefore()` . So for media,` moveBefore()` matters when the player is embedded in an` <iframe>` , such as a third-party video embed, and not for native media elements.


## moveBefore() Errors and Constraints


` moveBefore()` is stricter than` insertBefore()` . It throws in cases where` insertBefore()` would quietly do a remove-and-insert.


Error Triggered when What to do


` HierarchyRequestError` Moving between a connected and a disconnected tree Use` insertBefore()`


` HierarchyRequestError` Moving between documents Use` insertBefore()` (or` adoptNode()` first)


` HierarchyRequestError` Moving a node into its own descendant Fix the target: this is a logic bug


` HierarchyRequestError`` movedNode` is not an Element or CharacterData Use` insertBefore()`


` NotFoundError`` referenceNode` is not a child of the parent Pass a real child or` null`


` TypeError` The second argument is missing Pass` null` explicitly to append


The` TypeError` row catches people out because` insertBefore()` habits carry over: you cannot append by calling` moveBefore(node)` with only one argument.


## MutationObserver and connectedMoveCallback


A` MutationObserver` still records a node moved with` moveBefore()` as one removed node and one added node, so existing observers keep receiving records for moves. The DOM Standard’s[move steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#move) queue a removal record for the old parent and an addition record for the new one. Code that treats a removal as “destroyed” needs another signal if it should tell moves apart from deletions. For observer setup, see[the three DOM observer APIs](https://blog.openreplay.com/exploring-the-three-dom-observer-apis/) .


Custom elements get a dedicated move hook,` connectedMoveCallback()` . As[MDN’s custom elements guide](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_components/Using_custom_elements) explains, when` connectedMoveCallback()` is defined, it is called *instead of*` connectedCallback()` and` disconnectedCallback()` each time the element is moved to a different place in the DOM via` Element.moveBefore()` .


```text
class   DashCard   extends   HTMLElement   {
connectedCallback  ()     {   /* initial setup: subscriptions, timers */   }
disconnectedCallback  ()  {   /* teardown */   }
connectedMoveCallback  () {   /* runs instead of the two above on moveBefore() */   }
}
customElements  .  define  (  '  dash-card  '  ,   DashCard  );
```


If the class doesn’t define` connectedMoveCallback()` , a` moveBefore()` move still runs` disconnectedCallback()` and then` connectedCallback()` . Defining the method, even as an empty function, replaces that pair. The[HTML specification](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#preserving-custom-element-state-when-moved) covers this behavior.


## Feature Detection and Fallback for moveBefore


Check` 'moveBefore' in Element.prototype` before calling the method. Fall back to` insertBefore()` when the method is missing, and also when it throws a` HierarchyRequestError` for a move that` insertBefore()` would accept. Per[caniuse](https://caniuse.com/mdn-api_element_movebefore) , Chrome and Edge 133+ and Firefox 144+ support it, and Safari does not.[web-features](https://web-platform-dx.github.io/web-features-explorer/features/move-before/) lists it as Limited availability rather than Baseline.


```text
function   moveNode  (  parent  ,   node  ,   ref   =   null  ) {
if (  '  moveBefore  '   in   Element  .  prototype  ) {
try   {
parent  .  moveBefore  (  node  ,   ref  );
return  ;
}   catch   (  err  ) {
if (  err  .  name   !==   '  HierarchyRequestError  '  )   throw   err  ;   // NotFoundError etc. are real bugs
}
}
const   active   =   document  .  activeElement  ;
parent  .  insertBefore  (  node  ,   ref  );   // state-resetting path
if (  active   &&   node  .  contains  (  active  ))   active  .  focus  ();
}
```


The` insertBefore()` fallback still reloads iframes, restarts animations and closes dialogs, exactly as` insertBefore()` always has. Restoring focus only puts focus back, and caret position is not guaranteed. This check covers Element parents only. It does not tell you whether` Document` or` DocumentFragment` support the method.


## Conclusion


` moveBefore()` gives the DOM a true move for the first time: one call that keeps iframes loaded, focus in place and animations running, as long as you stay inside the constraints MDN lists. Find every` appendChild()` or` insertBefore()` call in your drag-and-drop or morphing code that moves a live node, send it through a helper like` moveNode()` , and add` connectedMoveCallback()` to any custom element whose setup shouldn’t run again when it’s repositioned.


## FAQs


Can moveBefore() move an element into or out of a shadow root?


Yes. ShadowRoot inherits from DocumentFragment, so it has its own moveBefore() method. The move must stay within the same shadow-including root, and a connected shadow root meets that requirement for any node connected to the same document. Moving light DOM content into a connected shadow tree keeps focus, iframe loading state and the other states MDN lists.


Why does moveBefore() throw when I insert a newly created element?


An element made with document.createElement() is not connected to the document yet. Moving a disconnected node into a connected parent throws a HierarchyRequestError. Use appendChild() or insertBefore() for the first insertion. A node that has never been connected has no iframe, focus or animation state to keep, so nothing is lost. Use moveBefore() only for moves after that.


Can moveBefore() be polyfilled for Safari?


No. A polyfill can add a moveBefore() method that calls insertBefore(), but that only copies the method name. The browser engine keeps iframe documents, focus, animations and open popovers alive during the move, and JavaScript cannot do that. In browsers without native support, a shim behaves exactly like insertBefore() and resets the same state.


Do any libraries already use moveBefore()?


Yes. htmx added moveBefore() support in version 2.0.3, released in October 2024. When the browser exposes moveBefore(), htmx uses it to move elements marked with hx-preserve during content swaps, so those elements keep their state. In browsers without the method, htmx goes back to its normal behavior, which moves elements the old remove-and-insert way.
